result.detailed_feedback:
**Element Layout (18.5 points):**
The video employs a highly effective split-screen layout, placing instructional text on the left and dynamic animations on the right. This spatial organization respects the learner's cognitive load by separating conceptual descriptions from visual demonstrations. The use of whitespace is excellent, preventing the screen from feeling cluttered even when complex graphs are displayed. Text and diagrams are sized appropriately for readability across various devices. A minor improvement could be made in the vertical alignment of text versus the graphs to ensure a more centered visual weight.

**Attractiveness (19.0 points):**
The aesthetic is modern and professional, utilizing a high-contrast 'dark mode' theme that makes the vibrant plot lines (greens, blues, and yellows) pop. The animation of the Riemann sums—where blocks transition into a smooth shaded area—is visually satisfying and engaging. The 'zooming' metaphor to explain derivatives is executed with smooth transitions that effectively capture the learner's attention.

**Logic Flow (19.5 points):**
The pedagogical progression is flawless. It begins with intuitive 'Prerequisites' (motion), moves to a geometric definition of derivatives, transitions to the concept of integration as accumulation, and culminates in the 'Grand Connection.' The sequence mirrors the historical and logical development of calculus, building complexity through scaffolding. The transition from the velocity graph to the area function is a masterclass in instructional sequencing.

**Accuracy & Depth (19.0 points):**
The content is mathematically rigorous yet accessible. It accurately identifies the derivative as the slope/rate and the integral as the area/accumulation. Crucially, it visualizes the Area Function (A'(x) = f(x)), which is the most difficult part of the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus for students to grasp. The inclusion of the '+ C' in the symbolic representation shows attention to detail often missed in short summaries.

**Visual Consistency (19.0 points):**
The video maintains a strict visual language. Color-coding is consistent throughout: for example, when the text mentions 'velocity,' the corresponding graph element uses the same blue hue. Typography is uniform, and the animation speed remains constant, providing a cohesive experience that allows the learner to focus on the concepts rather than the interface.

**Overall Summary:**
This is an exceptional educational video that provides a clear and visually compelling explanation of the relationship between integrals and derivatives. Its greatest strength lies in its ability to bridge the gap between geometric intuition (slopes and areas) and formal mathematical relationships through the 'Area Function' demonstration. It is highly suitable for high school or early college calculus students.

**Key Strengths:**
• Expert use of color-coding to link text descriptions with visual elements.
• Highly effective visualization of Riemann sums transitioning into a definite integral.
• Clear demonstration of the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus via the moving Area Function.
• Excellent pacing that allows for conceptual absorption without stagnation.

**Areas for Improvement:**
• Explicitly name 'The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus' during the 'Grand Connection' phase for better academic indexing.
• The character 'Leo the Lion' is a bit stylistically detached from the professional look of the coordinate planes; a more abstract or sleek avatar might fit the aesthetic better.
• Provide a brief final slide with the formal mathematical notation of the FTC for students to reference.

The area under a rate-versus-time graph represents the total accumulated quantity. In this case, the flow rate (volume/time) is plotted against time, so the area under the curve calculates the total volume of water added to the tank over that time period.
